claim: A CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen of 1213 mouse RBPs was performed to identify their ability to affect proliferation and/or survival, and the abundance of differentiated CD138+ cells in vitro.
source: To identify roles of RNA binding proteins (RBPs) in the differentiation or survival of antibody secreting plasma cells we performed a CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen of 1213 mouse RBPs for their ability to affect proliferation and/or survival, and the abundance of differentiated CD138 + cells in vitro.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the experimental approach and the number of RBPs screened.

claim: CSDE1 promotes the accumulation of CD138+ cells in vitro.
source: We validated the binding partners CSDE1 and STRAP as well as the m6A binding protein YTHDF2 as promoting the accumulation of CD138 + cells in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states validation of CSDE1 as promoting CD138+ cell accumulation.

claim: STRAP promotes the accumulation of CD138+ cells in vitro.
source: We validated the binding partners CSDE1 and STRAP as well as the m6A binding protein YTHDF2 as promoting the accumulation of CD138 + cells in vitro.

claim: YTHDF2 promotes the accumulation of CD138+ cells in vitro.
source: We validated the binding partners CSDE1 and STRAP as well as the m6A binding protein YTHDF2 as promoting the accumulation of CD138 + cells in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states validation of YTHDF2 as promoting CD138+ cell accumulation.

claim: EIF3K inhibits CD138+ cell accumulation in vitro.
source: We validated the EIF3 subunits EIF3K and EIF3L and components of the CCR4-NOT complex as inhibitors of CD138 + cell accumulation in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states validation of EIF3K as inhibiting CD138+ cell accumulation.

claim: EIF3L inhibits CD138+ cell accumulation in vitro.

evidence: The abstract states validation of EIF3L as inhibiting CD138+ cell accumulation.

claim: Components of the CCR4-NOT complex inhibit CD138+ cell accumulation in vitro.

evidence: The abstract states validation of CCR4-NOT complex components as inhibiting CD138+ cell accumulation.

claim: YTHDF2-deficient plasma cells failed to accumulate in chimeric mouse models.
source: In chimeric mouse models YTHDF2-deficient plasma cells failed to accumulate.
evidence: The abstract states the in vivo finding from chimeric mouse models.

claim: Humoral immunity requires the generation of antibody-secreting plasmablasts and plasma cells.
source: Humoral immunity requires the generation of antibody-secreting plasmablasts and plasma cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about humoral immunity.

claim: Antibody secreting cells are derived from naive B cell precursors that enter the extrafollicular response and the germinal centre (GC) reaction.
source: These are derived from naive B cell precursors that enter the extrafollicular response and the germinal centre (GC) reaction (Nutt et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nutt et al., 2015.

claim: Germinal centre derived antibody secreting cells may migrate to the bone marrow where they survive as long-lived plasma cells secreting high-affinity antibody.
source: Germinal centre derived antibody secreting cells may migrate to the bone marrow where they survive as long-lived plasma cells secreting high-affinity antibody.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about plasma cell biology.

claim: The B- to plasma-cell transition requires substantial reprogramming of the transcriptome.
source: The B- to plasma-cell transition requires substantial reprogramming of the transcriptome.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about B cell differentiation.

claim: Transcriptome reprogramming during B- to plasma-cell transition is achieved in part by the actions of transcription factors and epigenetic regulators.
source: This is achieved in part by the actions of transcription factors and epigenetic regulators that act within a layered system to control the timing of differentiation and its coordination with extracellular cues.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about gene regulation during differentiation.

claim: Mir148a promotes plasma cell differentiation.

claim: Mir155 promotes plasma cell differentiation.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lu et al., 2014.

claim: Mir125b suppresses plasma cell differentiation.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gururajan et al., 2010.

claim: RNA binding proteins (RBPs) act co- or post-transcriptionally to influence the quality and quantity of expressed genes.
source: RNA binding proteins (RBPs) act co- or post-transcriptionally to influence the quality and quantity of expressed genes.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about RBP function.

claim: Estimates of the numbers of RBPs encoded in the mammalian genome vary between one to five thousand.
source: However, while estimates of the numbers of RBPs encoded in the mammalian genome vary between one to five thousand, few have been implicated in plasma cell differentiation, survival, and migration.

claim: Few RBPs have been implicated in plasma cell differentiation, survival, and migration.
source: However, while estimates of the numbers of RBPs encoded in the mammalian genome vary between one to five thousand, few have been implicated in plasma cell differentiation, survival, and migration.

claim: HNRNPLL promotes differentiation indirectly by suppressing BCL6 expression.
source: These include, HNRNPLL which promotes differentiation indirectly by suppressing BCL6 expression (Chang et al., 2015); the non-canonical poly(A) polymerase FAM46C/TENT5C which acts as a tumour suppressor in myeloma (Bilska et al., 2020); and ZFP36L1 which is required for the emigration of plasma cells (Saveliev et al., 2021).

claim: FAM46C/TENT5C acts as a tumour suppressor in myeloma.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bilska et al., 2020.

claim: ZFP36L1 is required for the emigration of plasma cells.

claim: The study identified 103 RBPs that promote CD138+ cell abundance.

claim: The study identified 189 RBPs that inhibit CD138+ cell abundance.
source: We identified 103 RBPs that promote and 189 RBPs that inhibit plasma cell abundance and validated some of these using follow up assays with independent single guide RNA (sgRNA) sequences.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results.

claim: YTHDF2, an N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification binding protein, acting within B cells is necessary for the accumulation of plasma cells in the bone marrow.
source: Using mouse models, we demonstrated that YTHDF2, an N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification binding protein, acting within B cells is necessary for the accumulation of plasma cells in the bone marrow.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the in vivo experimental findings.

claim: The custom sgRNA library was constructed in a vector backbone expressing puromycin resistance and CD90.1 as selection markers.
source: A custom sgRNA library targeting these was constructed in a vector backbone expressing puromycin resistance and CD90.1 as selection markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the construction of the screening library with reference to a figure.

claim: The library encodes 10 sgRNAs per gene.
source: The library encodes 10 sgRNAs per gene, targets 72 positive control genes and contains 500 negative control sgRNAs.
evidence: This describes the design of the sgRNA library.

claim: The library targets 72 positive control genes.
source: The library encodes 10 sgRNAs per gene, targets 72 positive control genes and contains 500 negative control sgRNAs.
evidence: This describes the design of the sgRNA library.

claim: The library contains 500 negative control sgRNAs.
source: The library encodes 10 sgRNAs per gene, targets 72 positive control genes and contains 500 negative control sgRNAs.

claim: The library contains 13,350 sgRNAs in total.
source: It contains 13,350 sgRNAs in total with >98.8% of sgRNAs normally distributed within a 16-fold range (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Supplementary file 1B).

claim: >98.8% of sgRNAs are normally distributed within a 16-fold range.
source: It contains 13,350 sgRNAs in total with >98.8% of sgRNAs normally distributed within a 16-fold range (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Supplementary file 1B).

claim: Primary mouse B cells expressing Cas9 from the Rosa26 locus were cultured in vitro on fibroblasts expressing CD40ligand and BAFF for 4 days with IL-4 followed by 4 days with IL-21.
source: To screen RBPs that regulate cell expansion (proliferation or survival), primary mouse B cells expressing Cas9 from the Rosa26 locus were cultured in vitro on fibroblasts expressing CD40ligand and BAFF for 4 days with IL-4 followed by 4 days with IL-2115.
evidence: This describes the experimental culture conditions for the screen.

claim: sgRNAs targeting Trp53 enriched as expected for inhibiting cell expansion.
source: sgRNAs targeting Trp53 and Myc enriched as expected for inhibiting and supporting cell expansion, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This describes the validation of the screen using known control genes.

claim: sgRNAs targeting Myc enriched as expected for supporting cell expansion.
source: sgRNAs targeting Trp53 and Myc enriched as expected for inhibiting and supporting cell expansion, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This describes the validation of the screen using known control genes.

claim: Rc3h1, Caprin1, and Fam46c were the only RBPs enriched for limiting B cell proliferation or survival.
source: Rc3h1, Caprin1, and Fam46c were the only RBPs enriched for limiting B cell proliferation or survival (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results.

claim: FAM46C has been implicated in impairing the proliferation and/or survival of B cells.
source: FAM46C has been implicated in impairing the proliferation and/or survival of B cells (Mroczek et al., 2017; Bilska et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mroczek et al., 2017 and Bilska et al., 2020.

claim: The role for Rc3h1 as limiting proliferation or survival was validated with individual sgRNAs.
source: Further supporting the predictive power of our dataset, we validated the role for Rc3h1 as limiting proliferation or survival with individual sgRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This describes validation experiments with individual sgRNAs.

claim: On day 8 of the culture, CD138+ cells co-express CD267, IRF4, and BLIMP1 (encoded by Prdm1).
source: On day 8 of the culture, we sorted cells based on the expression of CD138, a marker of differentiated plasma cells that co-express CD267, IRF4, and BLIMP1 (encoded by Prdm1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G), and determined the representation of sgRNAs by NGS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Supplementary file 1D).
evidence: This describes the characterization of CD138+ cells with reference to a figure.

claim: The transcription factors Bach2, Bcl6, Spi1, and Irf8 enriched for inhibiting CD138+ cell accumulation.
source: The transcription factors: Bach2, Bcl6, Spi1, and Irf8 enriched for inhibiting CD138 + cell accumulation, and Prdm1 enriched for promoting CD138 + cell accumulation, while Irf4 was required for CD138 + cell accumulation as well as B cell expansion (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

claim: Prdm1 enriched for promoting CD138+ cell accumulation.
source: The transcription factors: Bach2, Bcl6, Spi1, and Irf8 enriched for inhibiting CD138 + cell accumulation, and Prdm1 enriched for promoting CD138 + cell accumulation, while Irf4 was required for CD138 + cell accumulation as well as B cell expansion (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

claim: Irf4 was required for CD138+ cell accumulation as well as B cell expansion.
source: The transcription factors: Bach2, Bcl6, Spi1, and Irf8 enriched for inhibiting CD138 + cell accumulation, and Prdm1 enriched for promoting CD138 + cell accumulation, while Irf4 was required for CD138 + cell accumulation as well as B cell expansion (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

claim: The screening results for Bach2, Bcl6, Spi1, Irf8, Prdm1, and Irf4 are consistent with the established roles of these genes in B cells and plasma cells.
source: These results are consistent with the established roles (Bilska et al., 2020; Ochiai et al., 2008; Ochiai et al., 2006; Muto et al., 2010; Shaffer et al., 2000; Tunyaplin et al., 2004; Carotta et al., 2014; Shapiro-Shelef et al., 2003; Lin et al., 2002; Shaffer et al., 2002; Sciammas et al., 2006; Ochiai et al., 2013) of these genes in B cells and plasma cells, and therefore underpin our confidence that novel findings in this system reflect meaningful biological effects.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and serves as validation of the screening approach.

claim: CSDE1 and STRAP bind to each other.
source: We validated CSDE1 and STRAP which bind to each other (Hunt et al., 1999) as promoting CD138 + cell accumulation and the eIF3 octamer subunits eIF3K and eIF3L as limiting CD138 + cell accumulation (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hunt et al., 1999.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in eIF3K and eIF3L have previously been shown to extend Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan by enhancing resistance to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in eIF3K and eIF3L have previously been shown to extend Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan by enhancing resistance to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress (Cattie et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cattie et al., 2016.

claim: eIF3K and eIF3L may inhibit CD138+ cell appearance by limiting tolerance to ER stress.
source: Hence, eIF3K and eIF3L may inhibit CD138 + cell appearance by limiting tolerance to ER stress.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from prior knowledge.

claim: All three YTHDF-family members of m6A binding proteins were enriched for increasing CD138+ cell abundance.
source: All three YTHDF-family members of m6A binding proteins were also enriched for increasing CD138 + cell abundance (Figure 1D) of which Ythdf2 had the most pronounced effect (Figure 1E, F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

claim: Ythdf2 had the most pronounced effect among YTHDF-family members on CD138+ cell abundance.
source: All three YTHDF-family members of m6A binding proteins were also enriched for increasing CD138 + cell abundance (Figure 1D) of which Ythdf2 had the most pronounced effect (Figure 1E, F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

claim: ZFP36, an AU-rich element binding protein, was enriched for limiting CD138+ cell abundance.

claim: The TNRC6 family critical for miRNA mediated repression was enriched for limiting CD138+ cell abundance.
source: By contrast, ZFP36, an AU-rich element binding protein, and the TNRC6 family critical for miRNA mediated repression were enriched for limiting CD138 + cell abundance (Figure 1D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to figures.

claim: ZFP36 has been previously reported to limit CD138+ cell appearance in vitro.
source: ZFP36 has been previously reported to limit CD138 + cell appearance in vitro (Chu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chu et al., 2016.

source: The YTHDF-, ZFP36- and TNRC6-families of RBPs are all known to promote RNA decay by recruiting the CCR4-NOT complex leading to deadenylation and subsequent decay (Du et al., 2016; Fabian et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2014).

claim: The YTHDF-family suppress transcripts that inhibit plasma cell differentiation or survival.
source: In this model, we envisage the ZFP36- and TNRC6-families suppress transcripts that promote plasma cell differentiation or survival, while the YTHDF-family suppress transcripts that inhibit plasma cell differentiation or survival.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: Ythdf2 and its paralogues promote CD138+ cell accumulation, without appreciably affecting B cell expansion.
source: Our screen demonstrated that Ythdf2 and its paralogues promote CD138 + cell accumulation, without appreciably affecting B cell expansion.

source: Following anti-IgM stimulation in vitro the numbers of Ythdf2 CKO B cells at each division was not different from Ythdf2fl/fl control (Ythdf2 CTL) B cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).

claim: Ythdf2 CKO B cells generated fewer CD138+ cells compared to Ythdf2 CTL B cells.
source: Because Ythdf2 CKO B cells generated fewer CD138 + cells compared to Ythdf2 CTL B cells (Figure 1G), we hypothesise that YTHDF2 promotes B cell differentiation independently of a role in CSR, cell proliferation or survival, or specifically promotes the survival of differentiated CD138 + cells.

claim: YTHDF2 promotes B cell differentiation independently of a role in CSR, cell proliferation or survival, or specifically promotes the survival of differentiated CD138+ cells.
source: Because Ythdf2 CKO B cells generated fewer CD138 + cells compared to Ythdf2 CTL B cells (Figure 1G), we hypothesise that YTHDF2 promotes B cell differentiation independently of a role in CSR, cell proliferation or survival, or specifically promotes the survival of differentiated CD138 + cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a hypothesis based on the experimental results.

claim: Ythdf2-deficient cells efficiently reconstituted the splenic B cell pool in mixed bone-marrow chimeras.
source: Ythdf2-deficient cells efficiently reconstituted the splenic B cell pool (Figure 2A) enabling us to test the hapten-specific responses of mature B cells lacking YTHDF2 in two independent immunisation experiments with alum precipitated 4-Hydroxy-3-nitrophenylacetyl coupled to the carrier protein Keyhole-Limpet Hemocyanin (NP-KLH).

source: At 21 days after immunisation the ratio of high and low valency NP-binding IgG1 in Ythdf2 CKO chimeras was comparable to controls (Figure 2B), however, a slight defect may exist that remains undetected by the power of our experiment.

claim: A slight defect in the ratio of high and low valency NP-binding IgG1 may exist in Ythdf2 CKO chimeras that remains undetected by the power of the experiment.
source: At 21 days after immunisation the ratio of high and low valency NP-binding IgG1 in Ythdf2 CKO chimeras was comparable to controls (Figure 2B), however, a slight defect may exist that remains undetected by the power of our experiment.

evidence: This describes experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: At day 21, NIP+IgG1+ plasma cells in the bone marrow were threefold lower in the Ythdf2 CKO compared to the controls.
source: At day 21, the number of CD138 +CD267+ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) NIP +IgG1 + splenic plasmablasts (Figure 2C) and NIP +IgG1 + plasma cells in the bone marrow (Figure 2D) were both threefold lower in the Ythdf2 CKO compared to the controls.
evidence: This describes experimental results with reference to figures.

source: We observed no difference in CXCR4 expression in CD138 +CD267 + cells between genotypes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).

claim: >98% of YTHDF2-deficient cells in competitive chimeras were GFP negative and thus having undergone Cre-mediated deletion.
source: In our competitive chimeras, YTHDF2-deficient cells efficiently reconstituted the mature B cell pool (Figure 3A) with >98% being GFP negative and thus having undergone Cre-mediated deletion (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: At 21 days after immunisation, the number of NIP+IgG1+ splenic plasmablasts was fivefold lower in the Ythdf2 CKO chimeras compared to the controls.
source: At 21 days after immunisation, the number of NIP +IgG1 + splenic plasmablasts was fivefold lower in the Ythdf2 CKO chimeras compared to the controls (Figure 3B).

claim: There were similar numbers of CD45.1 B6.SJL-derived plasma cells in the bone marrow of Ythdf2 CTL and Ythdf2 CKO chimeras.

claim: There were similar numbers of NIP+IgG1+ plasma cells in the bone marrow of Ythdf2 CTL and Ythdf2 CKO chimeras.

evidence: This describes experimental results with reference to figures.
